cohort: 10,166 women giving birth at San José Hospital in Santiago, Chile, between March 2020 and August 2021
finding: Immigrant mothers in Santiago, Chile, during the COVID-19 pandemic experienced higher rates of c-sections, particularly emergency c-sections, and lower rates of personalized childbirth care and support compared to non-immigrant mothers.
mod_finding: Immigrant mothers had a higher proportion of c-sections, specifically emergency c-sections (28.64% vs. 21.10%; p-value < 0.001), compared to non-immigrant women. Haitians had the highest risk of undergoing emergency c-section (aRR = 1.61) and Venezuelans had the highest risk of elective c-section (aRR = 2.18) compared to non-immigrants.
